title: liquid-glass-react
lede: A React component library by Max Rovensky, published on npm on June 10, 2025, one day after Apple announced Liquid Glass.
summary: The first popular web reimplementation of Liquid Glass, as React components. 2025.
made: 2025 (npm 0.0.1 published June 10, 2025; repository last pushed June 13, 2025)

evidence.note: Inspected the repository file assets/card.png (1296 × 736) in a scratchpad copy. Not stored.

styles.note: Partial fit. It carries the lensing glass to the web, but it puts content in a glass card, which Apple’s guidelines reserve for controls.

context: The repository describes itself as “Apple’s Liquid Glass effect for React”, under the MIT license, with about 6,300 GitHub stars when checked. [GitHub](https://github.com/rdev/liquid-glass-react).

Wikipedia calls it the earliest web implementation and the most downloaded Liquid Glass package on npm, and says that its development stopped shortly after release. [Wikipedia: Liquid Glass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquid_Glass).
observed: A warm, sepia photo of a ruined pier over the sea with gulls fills the frame.
A rounded glass card in the middle holds a “User Info” profile: initials in a circle, a name, and three label-value rows in white sans-serif.
Through the card the pier is heavily blurred and warmed to amber, and the dark pier struts smear sideways near the left edge of the card.
The card has a thin light rim, slightly brighter on its upper edge, and a soft shadow.
interpretation: The demo blends the two styles: Liquid Glass edge distortion, but glassmorphism’s content card with strong blur.
borrow: Raise the blur under text-bearing glass and keep the refraction for the rim.

rights.statement: The code is MIT (© 2025 Max Rovensky). Kept as link only because the demo image shows a third-party photograph whose license is not stated.
